## Code Review Findings

**Files reviewed**: 5 candidate files and 1 historical snapshot; 25 lines changed across 2 files (21 insertions, 4 deletions).
**Active profiles**: python
**Overall assessment**: APPROVE
**Intent and scope**: Explicit [README contract](/tmp/kk-isolated-review-zvHtbV/candidate/README.md:5): trim preference IDs before lookup while preserving resilient reads. Reviewed the supplied staged diff and complete candidate snapshots. No task scope or pending-task exclusions.
**Baselines**: Review base `7c0410c18bac40c33f857000ac3cc59d38a02165`; candidate is the supplied immutable index snapshot identified in [provenance.json](/tmp/kk-isolated-review-zvHtbV/provenance.json). No separate released/deployed baseline or release assessment.

### Behavior and Compatibility

**Supported:** The public path remains `Preferences.read → read_preferences → Repository.read_resilient → read_once → ScriptedBackend.read`. [reader.py:2](/tmp/kk-isolated-review-zvHtbV/candidate/reader.py:2) normalizes once before entering the unchanged [retry policy](/tmp/kk-isolated-review-zvHtbV/candidate/repository.py:29), so every attempt receives the same normalized ID.

| Scenario | Expected and candidate behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Unpadded or whitespace-padded ID; immediate success | Return the first result after one normalized lookup | Reader source; stored trim test; parent-attributed checks |
| One transient failure, then success | Retry with the same normalized ID; return attempt 2 | Retry source; stored transient test |
| Two transient failures, then success | Return attempt 3; make no further attempt | Retry source; parent-attributed check |
| Three transient failures | Propagate the third exception after exactly three attempts | Bare re-raise in retry source; stored limit test; parent-attributed identity check |
| Immediate `MissingPreference` | Propagate after one attempt | Specific transient catch; stored permanent-error test |
| Transient failure, then `MissingPreference` | Propagate the permanent error on attempt 2 | Retry source; parent-attributed check |
| Immediate success followed by a scripted error; empty result | Stop at first success, including an empty dictionary | Unconditional return; parent-attributed checks |

Historical comparison inspected repository `/tmp/fr-opus55-matrix-20261011/codex-candidate-R9-recovery-isolated-1`, revision `7c0410c18bac40c33f857000ac3cc59d38a02165`, original `reader.py`, lines 1–2 ([materialized source](/tmp/kk-isolated-review-zvHtbV/historical/reader.py:1)). The candidate adds normalization while preserving delegation to `read_resilient`. The unchanged public caller and repository interfaces remain compatible.

No business writes or new persistent state were introduced. Scripted outcome consumption and attempt recording remain fixture behavior.

**Not applicable:** Deployment, migration, activation and mixed-service compatibility; the documented component uses a local scripted backend.

Parent reports all four unit tests and seven additional scenario checks passed against matching worktree/index content. These are attributed execution results; I independently inspected source and did not execute tests.
